title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 14 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 14)

content.overview: Section 14 provides for termination of an arbitrator's mandate where the arbitrator becomes de jure or de facto unable to perform functions or fails to act without undue delay, and also where the arbitrator withdraws or the parties agree to termination.
content.glance: Section 14 provides for termination of an arbitrator's mandate where the arbitrator becomes de jure or de facto unable to perform functions or fails to act without undue delay, and also where the arbitrator withdraws or the parties agree to termination.
content.study:
Section 14 — Failure or impossibility to act

An arbitrator's mandate terminates where the arbitrator becomes de jure or de facto unable to perform functions or fails to act without undue delay. The mandate also terminates where the arbitrator withdraws from office or the parties agree to termination.

Where a controversy remains concerning one of the statutory grounds, a party may apply to the Court to decide termination of the mandate, subject to the statutory conditions. Section 14 must be distinguished from section 13: section 13 is the challenge procedure, whereas section 14 addresses inability, failure or termination of mandate.
